title: Optimize Autopilot Commit Validator and Canary Circuit
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a commit-time validator and runtime canary circuit for automatic application of Optimize suggestions (batching/caching recommendations). Goal is to let Optimize autopilot apply safe heuristics while preventing regressions and enabling fast rollback. The feature surfaces three components: (1) a pre-apply validator that simulates config changes against a lightweight cost/latency model and checks policy constraints; (2) a canary controller that ships changes gradually (by customer segment, traffic percentage, and region) with automated health checks and statistical checks for quality/regressions; (3) an operations approval and override UI that shows suggested delta, expected savings, risk flags, and one-click abort/revert.
acceptance_criteria: Validator runs in CI and rejects changes that violate configured SLO regressions or security policies
Canary controller can target 1%, 5%, 25% increments and perform automated rollback on thresholds
Dashboard shows pre-change simulation, live canary metrics (latency P95, error rate, token cost), and auto-generated revert link
Operator can approve, pause, or abort a rollout; abort triggers fast revert to previous effective config
End-to-end tests in staging prove KV-cache warmup behavior and avoid caching-induced correctness regressions

implementation_notes: Validator will use a sample-based estimator: pull 500 recent requests per route and run a fast simulation with quantized kernels to predict latency/cost impact
Policy layer: checks include min_throughput, max_p95_latency_delta (default 10%), no-cache-for-sensitive-routes flag
Canary controller: kickoff -> 1% for 10m -> 5% for 30m -> 25% for 1h -> full, with automated statistical tests (two-sided NAF) on latency and correctness
Circuit breaker: on trigger (latency > threshold OR error delta > threshold OR model-quality-alert), immediately cut traffic to previous config and mark rollout as failed
Telemetry: emit rollout events, per-key token cost deltas, warmup curves for KV cache, and a confidence metric calculated from sample variance
Backwards-compat: changes applied via config layers so revert is a single config patch; ensure migrations are idempotent
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Cache warmup causing transient QoS regressions when moving to more aggressive caching. Mitigation: gradual cache population window and synthetic warmup requests during canary
Risk: Statistical false positives on low-traffic customers. Mitigation: minimum-sample-size gating and fallback to manual approval for customers under threshold
Risk: Rollout revert latency too high for large fleets. Mitigation: precompute revert plan and provide a hot path in the config-sync agent for fast rollbacks
Risk: Unauthorized autopilot commits. Mitigation: require ops approval for changes that exceed 'auto-apply budget' and log audit trail
